title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 68
paragraphs: Thus he dealt with Adrastus. He also changed the names of the Dorian tribes, so that the Sicyonians might not have the same tribes as the Argives—in which he showed great contempt for the Sicyonians, for the names he gave them were taken from the names of a pig and an ass, altering only the endings, except in the case of his own tribe, to which he gave a name derived from his own rule. These last, then, were called Archelai (“rulers of the people”); the others of one tribe were called Hyatai (“pig-men”), another Oneatai (“ass-men”), and the remaining tribe Choireatai (“swine-men”). These tribe-names were used by the Sicyonians not only in the reign of Cleisthenes but also for sixty years after his death. Then, however, they reconsidered the matter and changed them to Hylleis, Pamphyli, and Dymanatae, adding a fourth to these, to which they gave the name Aegialeis, after Aegialeus the son of Adrastus.
